text.p: Strong full-year results from British health and technology group Amersham International Plc on June 10 will be watched for news of progress on talks to merge its life science division with Pharmacia Biotech, analysts said on Friday.

Amersham admitted last week it was talking to Swedish-U.S. group Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc about merging their life sciences operations to create a major international player in drug discovery technology.
The company was believed to have planned an announcement with its full-year results, but was forced into an early admission after Amersham officials were spotted in Stockholm.

Analysts expect pre-tax profit in the year through March to leap by nearly a third, with forecasts ranging from 64.0 million stg to 66.5 million compared with 50.8 million a year earlier. The dividend is seen rising to between 21.0 and 22.0 pence from 18.0 pence.

Profits will be driven mainly by Amersham's healthcare division, which specialises in radiochemicals for disease diagnosis and treatment, and a steady pick-up at life sciences, where Amersham is increasingly targeting drug discovery technology.

In a note on the company published on Friday, analysts at BZW predicted a 30 percent rise in pre-tax profits to 66 million stg. BZW said the advance would be driven by heart-imaging agent Myoview, with sales predicted to jump 107 percent to 23 million stg, and profits flowing from its Japanese joint venture, Nihon Medi-Physics (NMP).
But BZW said it expected a sharp rise in Amersham's tax charge to limit the rise in earnings per share to around 17 percent.
Lehman Brothers analyst Stewart Adkins said, however, that news of the mooted joint venture with Pharmacia Biotech would be the main focus of interest.
Amersham would need to "have a decent explanation" for the move, Adkins said, which could tie its world-leading gene-sequencing skills to one particular type of hardware.

Analysts generally said there was a great deal of uncertainty about how Amersham would put together any link with Pharmacia Biotech, which has larger sales than Amersham Life Science but is thought to be less profitable.

The companies may form a separate joint venture company, which one analyst said could eventually be floated off as a separate business, leaving Amersham to focus on its promising healthcare operation.
